# derived from monero v0.18.5.1 source, not captured from a run
# fields: COMMAND_RPC_AUTO_REFRESH::response_t, src/wallet/wallet_rpc_server_commands_defs.h:2093-2097
#         -- EMPTY. The JSON-RPC result is {}.
# request: { enable bool (OPT true, :2087), period u32 seconds (OPT 0, :2088) } (:2081-2090).
# fmonero SENDS { enable: true, period: 20 } IMMEDIATELY AFTER EVERY SUCCESSFUL open_wallet, as step
#         four of wallet_session::open (§4.1, §5b), so the setting is EXPLICIT rather than inherited.
#         20 is DEFAULT_AUTO_REFRESH_PERIOD (src/wallet/wallet_rpc_server.cpp:63) -- the upstream
#         default, deliberately NOT raised.
# THE THROTTLE WORKS THE OPPOSITE WAY ROUND FROM THE OBVIOUS READING (§2d): while the wallet is
#         behind the tip it keeps blasting through block chunks on the SAME THREAD that serves RPC
#         (the server runs one thread: :291-292, under upstream's own comment "DO NOT START THIS
#         SERVER IN MORE THEN 1 THREADS WITHOUT REFACTORING"), and yields the RPC thread for only
#         auto_refresh_evaluation_ms + 100 ms (200-300 ms) once per WHOLE period of uninterrupted
#         syncing (:215, :257-280, the yield computed at :270-276). A LARGER period therefore means
#         LONGER blocking bursts and fewer of them: period 30 would have made the stall it is supposed
#         to mitigate measurably worse. The real mitigation is §2d's wallet_syncing classification.
# NOT IN DESIGN.md §8's deliverable list; added by Phase 0 with its reason recorded in
